elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.2: "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, for any reasons..." The commencing-on-the-later-of trigger tied to First Commercial Sale of both Products is deleted, so the right is unconditional and exercisable throughout the term. This is a licence agreement with no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is not borne out on the operative text, which expressly grants Ono a for-convenience right; the check appears keyed to different phrasing (e.g., a notice-adjacency pattern) rather than substance.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array" replaces the redacted [ * ] notice figure; 30 days is at the preferred threshold. The retained rationale-accompaniment formality is a delivery formality, not an additional condition precedent or longer period.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "and Array shall refund to Ono on a pro rata basis any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination." Pro rata is expressly stated (not merely inferred from post-termination coverage), the payer is Vendor (Array), and the trigger is Ono's convenience termination under 13.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met in the retained text: 13.3 is a cause-based mutual right conditioned on material breach and cure ("in the event the other Party shall have materially breached or defaulted... and such default shall have continued for ninety (90) days"); 13.5(a) confers Safety/Efficacy termination on Ono alone; the only other Array exits identified are bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2), each cause-based. No at-will Array exit appears in the record, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the literal 60-90 day fallback band (and better for Customer). Fallback level is therefore incomplete, but this is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: revised 13.2 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, or contingent payment on Ono for exercising the convenience right, so there is nothing to cap. Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee is a pre-existing consideration term, not a termination penalty.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply and is exceeded: Array has no convenience right at all (13.3 breach, 13.4 bankruptcy, 8.2 Competing Product breach are all cause-based), which is stricter than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Array convenience termination right exists to which a notice period could attach; the 90-day period in 13.3 is a breach cure period, not convenience notice.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met on the operative text (unconditional convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, and no Vendor at-will exit anywhere in Article 13).

The failed deterministic check ("Customer convenience termination present") does not survive substantive inspection - revised 13.2 states in terms that Ono "shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time" - so it is a pattern-matching artefact rather than a drafting defect.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to 13.2, deletes only the commencement trigger that blocked the right (necessary to reach element 1), fixes the redacted notice figure, and adds the refund sentence required by element 3. Favourable retained language ("for any reasons", the rationale formality) survives verbatim; 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 are untouched.

No model-language extras were imported: "in whole or in part" was correctly dropped (no Order Form or partial-termination structure), and no survival tail, expense allocation, or transition procedure was added.

Intent preserved: the pro rata refund reaches only period-allocated prepayments, so it does not contradict Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created. The Section 8.2 Competing Product tail, which keys a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term and can now bite earlier, is correctly flagged for separate handling rather than bundled into this redline - confirm it is in fact raised, since leaving it unaddressed is a commercial (not drafting) exposure.

No repair is required for T4C. If Array pushes back, the negotiable retreat is the fallback band (60-90 days) plus a fee cap of no more than three months' fees, but do not concede a Vendor convenience right.
